profile.entities: Khadim India Limited (Parent); KSR Footwear Limited (Demerged Manufacturing/Distribution Entity)
profile.subseg: Mass Value Footwear; Premium Formal (British Walkers); Athleisure; Franchise Model (TFM/FRM)
profile.themes: Inventory Rationalization; Premiumization Mix Shift; Store Rationalization; Demerger Execution

deepdive.sec: Footwear Retail / Mass-Market Value & Premium Hybrid

bull_bear.body: Deleveraging priority evident via trade payable reduction (INR 196 Cr to INR 111 Cr) and inventory drawdown; Demerger proceeds/structure aimed at optimizing balance sheet; No dividend commentary; Focus on funding working capital for new season stock.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Persistent demand weakness in mass segment; Political turmoil in key Eastern markets (Bengal/Assam elections impacted Q1); Raw material volatility (petroleum-based inputs); Execution risk in transitioning franchisee debtors; Structural limit on athleisure due to small store formats.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; Acknowledges self-inflicted pain from inventory correction; Disciplined on cost and working capital; Realistic about 1-2 quarter lag for recovery to reflect in numbers; Defensive on premium transition (maintaining mass base).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Athleisure growth is structurally capped not by demand but by physical store constraints (lack of changing rooms prevents women's category entry); The 40% inventory cut caused lost sales of INR 10-15 Cr in H2, creating a low base for FY27; Demerger was a key driver for the sharp drop in trade payables and cash, not just operational changes.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: TFM portfolio grew 46% YoY; British Walkers grew 6% YoY; Skechers showing sequential growth; Athleisure limited by store size (no changing rooms); Premium (>INR 1,500) contributes ~15% of revenue with 2-3% higher gross margin than mass segment.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw material costs up 20-25% pressuring margins for players unable to pass on prices | Khadim India Limited | beneficiary | Med | Management successfully implemented INR 25-50 price hikes and is shifting mix to premium segments which have lower discounting, potentially outperforming peers stuck in deep discounting cycles. |
| Small store formats limit category expansion (athleisure/women's) | Khadim India Limited | loser | High | Unlike larger format competitors, Khadim cannot capture the high-growth women's athleisure segment due to lack of changing rooms, capping total addressable market per store. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin compressed due to price cuts on sub-INR 500 products and clearance sales; Expected 50 bps recovery in FY27 via premium mix and reduced discounting; Raw material costs up 20-25% recently, partially offset by INR 25-50 MRP hikes; Operating deleverage evident as sales fell 12% while fixed costs remained sticky.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: FY27 Revenue: ~INR 400 Cr; EBITDA Margin: ~14%; Gross Margin: 49-50% (up 50 bps); Store Count: Stabilize around 200 COCO + franchise network; Capex: Focused on stock investment for TFM/FRM models rather than heavy COCO capex.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Not applicable for retail model; Inventory levels reduced ~40% YoY; Management indicates pipeline stock arriving in Q1 FY27 to support INR 400 Cr run-rate.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: E-commerce targeting >5% contribution (up from 3-4%); Franchise-led expansion (TFM/FRM) offering better capital efficiency than COCO; Premium brand penetration (British Walkers, Sharon) to drive ASP and margin mix.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Khadim India completed a painful inventory and store cleanup in FY26, resulting in a 12% revenue decline and sub-1% PAT, but management guides for a FY27 stabilization at INR 400 Cr revenue with 14% EBITDA margins driven by reduced discounting and a higher premium mix. The strategic demerger of manufacturing sharpens focus on asset-light retail expansion, though near-term growth is capped by small store formats limiting athleisure penetration.
